description:
Problem: on 2026-10-24 a comment-cleanup scope entry naming a file that does not exist (the TPC-DS EULA notice path _binaries/tpc-ds/templates/query_templates/EULA.txt; the file is at benchbox/_binaries/tpc-ds/templates/query_templates/EULA.txt) merged to develop in commit 39a942435ae7fe9fc78afabb3a0182b0bbf4c317 (#3168). The trusted comment-policy check reads the scope policy from the base, so the PR's own new entry was never checked for validity. Once merged, every PR's comment-policy job, and with it the required tooling check, failed against the broken base. Develop stayed wedged until #3385 merged with tooling briefly removed from the required checks by the owner. GitHub issue #3386 records the gap.

Outcome: the trusted checker validates the candidate policy (the committed tree, or the index under --staged) for structure. Listed notices, payloads and external selectors name paths tracked at the head; notice digests and byte ranges match the head bytes; schema, owner and evidence fields are valid. The head policy gains no authority: exclusions and authorization stay base-derived.

Constraint: CI and the pre-commit hook copy the checker from the base commit (scripts/run_comment_policy.py TRUSTED_FILES; ci.yml comment-policy job). The new validation therefore protects PRs whose base contains it, not the PR that adds it. All replays must invoke the candidate branch's scripts/check_comment_policy.py directly, not through run_comment_policy.py.

Decision gates:
1. Validity, not authority. Base-derived exclusions and authorization stay base-only. The head policy is checked for validity but never used to exempt source in its own PR. Stop if a design would let the head policy change what is exempt in its own PR.
2. Reuse, don't fork. Extend head_policy() (check_comment_cleanup_scope.py:351) and validate_head_token_evidence() (:356). That function already validates directives and obligations at the head. Add notices, payloads and external selectors, reusing validate_candidate_notices() (:1668-1698) and the field checks of validate_evidence() (:412-446) against head bytes. Do not reuse the full ledger command (main with --task-set): it reports obsolete SCOPE001 coverage findings (docs/internal/comment-cleanup-scope.md:39-43). Re-locate these line numbers before editing.
3. Placement. Run it inside the existing trusted checker, which the comment-policy job feeds into the required tooling check, and inside the local hook. Stop and ask the owner if it would add or rename a required context, or change ci.yml or run_comment_policy.py.
4. Trusted-file closure. Keep the change inside files already listed in TRUSTED_FILES. Stop if the change needs a new import of any repository module outside that list: after merge the base copy could not import it, and every PR would fail.
5. Current tip. Before opening the PR, run the new validation on the current develop tip. Stop and report if it fails, because develop already holds an invalid entry.

Item guardrails: comment-policy enforcement stays blocking. Add no new exemptions or fixture entries to get green. Make no ruleset edits. The reviewed-path refusal of notice paths not pinned at the base (check_comment_cleanup_scope.py:1804-1807) stays.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings in code; commits, PR bodies and docs carry no tracker item IDs or session labels; timing uses benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time().
